title: Heat sent on for reuse
alt: A face-on section of three rooms in a row: the data hall, the heat-recovery room and the pool hall. In the hall the in-row coolers pick up the servers' heat; a coolant distribution unit sends warm water out in a round violet pipe. In the heat-recovery room a plate heat exchanger passes the heat to another loop without mixing the two, and a heat pump raises its temperature; cooled water goes back to the hall in a round blue pipe. The pool's heating loop, violet, enters the pool at an inlet below the water surface. In the pool hall the basin is drawn in section with a deck at each side, a water surface with a light ripple, swimmers with heads and shoulders above the water, and violet warmth rising from the water.
sources: Water leaving an air-cooled hall about 18 degrees C: NREL / US DOE FEMP 2024
Heat pump output about 70 degrees C: Sabroe DualPAC 716-W, 50 to 70 degrees C (maker figure)

steps.caption: Three rooms in a row: the data hall, the heat-recovery room, and the pool hall next door.
In the hall, the in-row coolers pick up the servers’ heat in water. A coolant distribution unit sends that warm water out of the hall.
In the heat-recovery room, a plate heat exchanger passes the heat to another loop of water without mixing the two. A heat pump raises its temperature. The cooled water goes back to the hall.
The pool’s own heating loop carries the heat to the pool inlet.
The pool water stays warm. This pool centre uses about 455 to 663 MWh of heat a year.
The whole path: heat from the servers, through the heat-recovery room, into the pool, and cooled water back to the hall.
